candidates.core_provocation: In the near future, people can store a final memory for strangers to witness after their death. A woman asks a stranger to view hers before undergoing a procedure that will erase it, but he sees himself killing her—even though they have never met.
candidates.why_interesting: The story creates immediate tension around whether a memory is evidence of the past, a warning about the future, or a carefully planted lie.

candidates.core_provocation: After an accident, a memory-repair service mistakenly gives two strangers each other’s most important memory. One now remembers committing a murder, while the other remembers being loved by a child who is not theirs; they have one hour to decide whether to restore their original memories.
candidates.why_interesting: It turns the familiar idea of lost memory into a concrete race against time about identity, guilt, and which life feels truly real.

parsed.reason_for_choice: The first premise has the clearest immediate hook: a stranger witnesses his own apparent murder of someone he has never met. Its small cast, single central mystery, and possible countdown make it especially effective for a tense short story.
